description: Geocaching combines navigation and outdoor ethics: safety and planning, cache etiquette, GPS and map-and-compass skills, finding caches, Travel Bugs, Cache In Trash Out, and planning a geohunt for younger Scouts.

safety.note: Geocache only with permission, a buddy and a plan; never bury a cache or hide one where searching could damage the land.

versions.label: Checked against official scouting.org excerpts (partial verification)

provenance.notes: Requirement numbering and topics were checked against excerpts of official Scouting America pages (scouting.org) returned by a search index on 2026-10-24. The pages themselves could not be opened from the build environment, so wording was not compared word for word and some sub-items may be summarized from partial excerpts. Summaries are ScoutPath's own words. Excerpts confirmed requirements 1 and 7–9; requirements 2–6 cover etiquette, terms and navigation but their exact numbering was not visible, so they are not outlined yet.

references.label: Official merit badge page (scouting.org Merit Badge Hub)

requirements.title: Safety and planning
requirements.summary: Likely hazards, first aid for common injuries, and planning a GPS outing.

requirements.title: Your first find
requirements.summary: Using a geocaching website, with permission, to find a public cache near you.

requirements.title: A geocaching project
requirements.summary: One option: Cache to Eagle, a Travel Bug, hiding and maintaining a cache, or a Cache In Trash Out event.

requirements.title: Leading a geohunt
requirements.summary: Planning a geohunt with several waypoints for a youth group.
